sources.title: A Sulfonated Tweezer-Shaped Receptor Selectively Recognizes Caffeine in Water.
limits: Water/D2O equilibria, not serum binding, human PK or sleep reversal.
Table 1 BC500 must not be substituted for a one-to-one Kd; paraxanthine is absent from that ligand panel.

sources.title: Selection of Aptamers for Sensing Caffeine and Discrimination of Its Three Single Demethylated Analogues.
limits: Official primary abstract plus author-repository metadata; full manuscript not downloaded.
Detection limit in diluted serum is neither Kd nor circulating drug neutralization.

sources.title: Exploiting conformational changes in a caffeine aptamer to engineer synthetic RNA devices.
limits: Cellular gene regulation and biochemical binding, not human pharmacological reversal.
Paraxanthine binding was not detected in the tested conditions; this is not an infinite-Kd estimate.

sources.title: Using the Intrinsic Fluorescence of DNA to Characterize Aptamer Binding.
limits: Failure of an intrinsic-fluorescence reporter is not evidence that the aptamer cannot bind caffeine.

sources.title: A novel caffeine dehydrogenase in Pseudomonas sp. strain CBB1 oxidizes caffeine to trimethyluric acid.
limits: Primary abstract only; Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500.
Caffeine-to-trimethyluric-acid conversion requires electron-acceptor chemistry; no oral human application established.

sources.title: Delineation of the caffeine C-8 oxidation pathway in Pseudomonas sp. strain CBB1 via characterization of a new trimethyluric acid monooxygenase and genes involved in trimethyluric acid metabolism.
limits: Primary abstract only; Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500.
Bacterial substrate conversion does not establish inactive or safe products in humans.

sources.title: Validation of caffeine dehydrogenase from Pseudomonas sp. strain CBB1 as a suitable enzyme for a rapid caffeine detection and potential diagnostic test.
limits: Beverage/milk diagnostic performance is ex vivo; it is not activity after administering an enzyme.
